title: Temporal Slice Scheduler: attention-aware phase splitting for predictable latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design + implement a scheduling policy that splits requests into temporal slices (prefill vs decode phases) and assigns execution windows based on attention-cost estimates and per-customer QoS weights. The goal is to provide predictable P50/P95 latency for latency-sensitive traffic while preserving overall throughput for bulk/throughput workloads. This ticket covers design, microbench harness, simulation, and a canary release in staging.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduler prototype (in canary runtime) that routes mixed workload traffic according to temporal-slice policy and attention-cost signals
Measured reduction in P95 latency for latency-tagged requests by >= 30% under the mixed benchmark compared to baseline fairshare scheduler
End-to-end integration tests covering phase splitting correctness, backpressure propagation, and kernel packing compatibility
Playbook for toggling policy and rolling back in case of regression
Documentation added to Console team docs and runtime runbook
notes: Key idea: instead of allocating GPU time by opaque token counts, estimate attention-cost (cross-attention + self-attention cost scaling with seq len and heads) per request and translate into temporal slices for prefill and decode with soft guarantees.

Temporal slice = contiguous execution window where a request's prefill or decode op is allowed to make forward progress; slices are scheduled interleaved to reduce head-of-line blocking from long-prefill requests.
Policy includes weighted QoS buckets (low-latency, standard, bulk). Each bucket gets a minimum slice frequency; weights adapt to queue pressure and historical tail latency.

Scheduler will emit hints to kernel selection layer: pack short-decode slices into small-batch kernels (FP16/4-bit) while scheduling long-prefill slices to kernels optimized for KV warmup and attention fusion.
We will expose a tuning knob: 'slice-duration-ms' and 'slice-decay-factor' to balance fairness vs throughput.

Compatibility: must interop with KV cache warming, prefix caching, and continuous batching path. If a request is cache-miss heavy, policy should favor prefill-first slices to populate KV quickly and avoid repeated work.
decisions: Use attention-cost heuristic composed of (seq_len^1.1 * heads_coeff + avg_cross_attention_frac) — empirical exponent chosen to penalize very long sequences
Prefer soft SLOs (slice-frequency guarantees) rather than hard preemption; avoid killing in-progress decode tokens unless safety thresholds are breached
Kernel packing will be signaled via a deterministic 'slice fingerprint' (short/medium/long) which maps to precompiled kernel selection sets
Initial rollout on staging will use conservative defaults: 8ms slice-duration, decay-factor 0.85, and three QoS buckets
